sepolia.note: Single-chain exercise: it measures real inclusion time and the gas of on-chain Groth16 verification, not cross-chain relay latency.

bee.note: queueing simulation; coordination time is measured (M); validator clustering is not tested

formula.note: transaction features simulated (S); zk verdicts come from the real Groth16 verifier (M); threshold chosen on a 30% calibration split, results on the 70% test split

calibrated.note: weights fitted on the calibration split only (logistic regression, non-negative, sum to 1); threshold lets 1% of legitimate calibration transactions through; evaluated on the same test split

repeatedSplits.note: each split fits and thresholds on its own 30% and tests on its own 70%; both variants use the same 1% rule

detection.note: transactions simulated (S); every score comes from the deployed contract (M)

speculativeTransactionHandler.note: The contract evaluates sum_j lambda_j exp(-beta d_ij^2) for caller-supplied weights with a 5-term series for exp(-z); it does not solve for the weights.

transactions.note: real Sepolia transactions; ms = send to receipt

zk.claim: Groth16 confirmation accepts valid transfers and rejects forged ones
zk.rule: all valid proofs verify; every tampered proof, altered public input and unsatisfiable witness is rejected

rbf.claim: Gaussian-RBF speculation predicts the next block state more accurately than a naive predictor
rbf.rule: bootstrap 95% CI of (RBF MAE - persistence MAE) lies entirely below zero for every target that is not saturated; entirely above zero for any such target = not supported. Comparison with the moving-average and linear baselines is reported but does not change the verdict

baseFee.excluded: saturated: repeating the last value is already within tolerance in 100.0% of blocks

dual.claim: The speculative leg of the dual transaction is usable sooner than the wait-then-relay baseline
dual.rule: speculative-visibility 95% interval lies below the baseline interval and every confirmable leg finalises with the correct value

detail.note: confirmed finality is slower than the baseline by the proof-generation time

bee.claim: Bee-algorithm routing balances validator load better than naive policies
bee.rule: Jain's index of the Bee policy exceeds random, round-robin and stake-weighted routing by more than the combined 95% intervals at every load (PASS), at some loads only (PARTIAL), or at none (NOT SUPPORTED). The greedy least-loaded policy is reported but not required

confidence.claim: The proof-of-confidence score filters bad transactions at a low false-positive cost
confidence.rule: ZK gate plus confidence threshold reaches TPR >= 0.90 with FPR <= 0.05 on the held-out split and the score has a higher AUC than reputation alone

confidenceFitted.claim: With weights fitted on a calibration split, the proof-of-confidence score filters bad transactions at a low false-positive cost
confidenceFitted.rule: mean over 30 random 30/70 splits: ZK gate plus confidence threshold reaches TPR >= 0.90 with FPR <= 0.05, and the AUC on the main split exceeds reputation alone. Weights and threshold use the calibration part only

contracts.claim: The deployed Sepolia contracts implement the behaviour the paper describes
contracts.rule: bytecode exists at each address, the confidence contract returns scores on the scale of its thresholds and reacts to the zk flag, and the on-chain RBF evaluation tracks exp(-z) on the supported range

findings: every score returned by the deployed ConfidenceScoreCalculator is below its own high-confidence threshold (unit mismatch)
the deployed thresholds flag fewer than half of the injected bad transactions
on-chain Gaussian evaluation departs from exp(-z) by more than 0.05 once beta*d^2 >= 3
